---
title: "Part 5 — Group rules of the road"
---

Put these in your project's README and hold each other to them.

## The seven rules

**1. Pull before you start. Push when you stop.**
: The single habit that prevents most pain. Check RStudio's Git pane arrows
  every time you sit down.

**2. `main` must always run.**
: Anyone should be able to pull `main` and render the report. If you break it,
  fixing it is your only priority. Nobody can work on a broken base.

**3. Work on a branch; a teammate merges your pull request.**
: Never merge your own. The five minutes a teammate spends reading your diff
  is the cheapest quality control available.

**4. Own your files.**
: Put the ownership table in the README. Conflicts need two people in the same
  lines — so mostly, do not be there.

**5. Commit small, commit often, say why.**
: One idea per commit. The message explains *why*, because the diff already
  shows *what*.

**6. Never commit anything you would not email to a stranger.**
: No patient data, no passwords, no API keys, no `.Renviron`. Git never
  forgets: deleting a file later does not remove it from the history, and a
  pushed secret must be treated as burned. Get `.gitignore` right first.

**7. Never `git push --force` on a shared branch.**
: It deletes your teammates' commits. If you think you need it, ask.

## Commit message shape

```
Short line saying what changed (under ~60 characters)

Then a blank line, then why — the reasoning, the alternative you rejected,
the thing that will not be obvious in six weeks.
```

Real example from this project:

> **Set up project skeleton for the git tutorial**
>
> The `.gitignore` excludes RStudio session state, rendered output and secrets,
> but deliberately keeps the 4 KB synthetic CSV so students see that "never
> commit data" is a judgement, not a rule.

## A README that makes the group work

```markdown
# Project title

One sentence on what this analyses.

## Who owns what
| File | Owner |
|------|-------|
| R/01-clean.R | A |
| R/02-describe.R | B |
| R/03-model.R | C |
| report.qmd, Interpretation | everyone |

## How to run it
Open the .Rproj in RStudio, then: quarto render report.qmd

## Where the data come from
Simulated by data-raw/00-simulate-data.R. No real people.
```

The ownership table is not bureaucracy. It is your conflict-avoidance
mechanism written down.

## What good looks like at the end of term

- 30–80 small commits, not 4 giant ones
- messages a stranger could follow
- every contribution went through a pull request someone else merged
- `main` renders on any group member's laptop
- no data file over a megabyte, no secrets, ever
- and when your report says a number, you can point at the commit that
  produced it

That last one is worth more than the version control. A project whose history
you can walk is a project whose results you can defend.
